verifies: Every allowable annual increase percentage used in the banking calculations, plus the official caution that only ONE of the two 1992-93 rates may be imposed.

title: Learn about rent increases in San Francisco
verifies: 1.6% current AGA; 60%-of-CPI basis; 7% ceiling context; once per 12 months; base rent only; no rounding up; 30-day / 90-day notice and +5 days if mailed; contents of the notice; use the percentage in effect on the effective date; rent increase license; no charge for an additional roommate; FOUR official worked examples used to self-test the calculator.

title: Banked rent increases
verifies: Banking mechanics: add percentages, do not compound, do not prorate; no limit on how much can be banked; banked increases do not expire during a tenancy; new owners may use them; they do NOT carry over to a new tenant; partial increases leave the remainder banked; notice must state which part is banked; official worked example ($1,300 -> $1,387.10).

title: Rent Board Rules and Regulations, Part IV - Rent Increases Not Requiring Approval
pub: SF Rent Board (sf.gov) - official regulation text
verifies: Sec. 4.10 Notice (disclosure of each component; non-conforming increase null and void); Sec. 4.12 Banking (CONTROLLING TEXT: 'A full 12 months must have elapsed...'; not compounded; not rounded up; half-percent good-faith readjustment; duty to identify the banked portion and dates); Sec. 4.15 Effect of Vacancy (the Ordinance does not regulate initial rent for a new tenancy).

title: Document 600 - Chapter 37, Residential Rent Stabilization and Arbitration Ordinance (compiled, amended 11/24/2024)
pub: City & County of San Francisco (sf.gov PDF)
verifies: Sec. 37.2 definitions (CPI, housing services, rent, rent increases, rental units and exclusions); Sec. 37.3(a)(8) petition required for any increase above those permitted; Sec. 37.3(a)(9) lead-remediation 10%/12-month cap; Sec. 37.3(a)(11) prohibition on increases for additional occupants; Sec. 37.3(b)(1)-(6) mandatory notice contents and 'Nonconforming Rent Increases... shall be null and void'; Sec. 37.3(c) subtenant rent limit; Sec. 37.3(d) Costa-Hawkins conformance; table of contents confirming Sec. 37.10B Tenant Harassment, Sec. 37.10C Use and Sale of Algorithmic Devices Prohibited (Ord. 224-24, eff. 10/14/2024) and Sec. 37.15 Reporting Obligations; Licensing.

title: Learn about San Francisco rental laws
verifies: Coverage test: units built on or before June 13, 1979 generally have both rent control and eviction protection; how to check the building's age; the categories that have eviction protection only; the eight categories entirely exempt from the Rent Ordinance; Rent Board counselor line 415-252-4600.

title: The Rent Board Housing Inventory (rent increase license)
verifies: All residential owners must report; a rent increase license is generated for tenant-occupied units; a current license must be on file BEFORE any annual or banked increase goes into effect; the notice is unenforceable without a license on the effective date; annual deadline March 1; no monetary penalty for late filing; submitted information is PUBLIC; tenants may search the portal; operative 7/1/2022 for non-condo buildings with 10+ units, reporting began 3/1/2023 for condos and buildings with fewer than 10 units.

title: Notice of Owner Noncompliance with Housing Inventory
verifies: A rent increase notice that goes into effect while the unit is unlicensed may be null and void (and may apply for multiple years); the tenant may be entitled to a refund; the license rules apply ONLY to rent-controlled units; tenant remedies (Form 354 petition / Form 361 summary petition).

title: The Rent Board Fee
verifies: 2026-2027 fee: $59.00 per dwelling unit, $29.50 per guest unit; deadline March 1; 5% late penalty per month capped at 15%; owner may recover 50% ($29.50/unit) from a tenant in occupancy as of November 1 of the applicable tax year; exemption request window; fee cycle timeline.

title: Replacement of Roommates
verifies: Tenants may generally replace departing roommates even against a lease; the 14-day written consent procedure and its time limits; the grounds on which a denial is reasonable (Rules 6.15A, 6.15B, 6.15D, 6.15E); occupancy limits by bedroom count; 'The landlord may not increase the rent for the unit based on the replacement of a departing tenant or the addition of new occupants, even if agreed to by the tenant'; market-rate reset only where ALL original tenants have permanently vacated and only subtenants who moved in on/after 1/1/1996 remain.

title: Rent Increases Under Section 6.14 And Costa-Hawkins
verifies: Rules & Regs Sec. 6.14: an unlimited increase on remaining occupants when the LAST original occupant vacates, and only if a written 6.14 notice was timely served on each subsequent occupant (generally 60 days is reasonable); Costa-Hawkins reaches only a lawful SUBTENANT or assignee who did not reside there before 1/1/1996; a CO-TENANT is never subject to it regardless of move-in date; no petition is required but a tenant may petition alleging an unlawful increase.

title: Landlord Petitions and Passthroughs
verifies: The exhaustive list of above-AGA increase mechanisms: capital improvement passthrough; operating and maintenance expense increase; special circumstances / comparable units; Proposition I past rent history; utility passthrough; Rules & Regs Sec. 1.21 (no tenant in occupancy); plus the elective Sec. 6.14 / Costa-Hawkins determination petition and the lawful-rent determination petition. Filing is free; tenants need not pay until the Board approves; approval is retroactive to the notice's effective date. Rent Board address: 25 Van Ness Ave, Suite 700.

title: Tenant petitions
verifies: Tenant remedies and forms: 352 decrease in housing services; 353 failure to repair and maintain; 354 unlawful rent increase / determination of lawful rent; 355-358 passthrough challenges; 359/360 subtenant claims; 361 tenant summary petition on an invalid notice; 362 wrongful eviction; 363 financial hardship. Filing is free; matters resolve by mediation or arbitration before an ALJ. JURISDICTION: the Rent Board does NOT adjudicate harassment, discrimination, retaliation or security deposits - those go to court or another forum.

title: Rent Board Referral Listing (free tenant legal services)
verifies: The official list of free tenant-side counselling and legal services a tenant can use to challenge an increase (Bay Area Legal Aid, Housing Rights Committee of SF, Eviction Defense Collaborative, SF Tenants Union, Causa Justa :: Just Cause, Tenderloin Housing Clinic, Open Door Legal, Advancing Justice-Asian Law Caucus, Legal Assistance to the Elderly, Chinatown CDC, SRO Collaboratives, Bar Association of SF Justice & Diversity Center / LARC). The Rent Board cannot refer to individual attorneys and no lawyer is needed to file a petition.

title: Allowable rent increases
verifies: The two inputs to any lawful increase (the published rate and the date of the last increase or lease start); the 12-month rule; base rent excludes passthrough charges; parking/storage generally IS base rent; increases are never automatic; 30/90-day notice plus 5 days if mailed.

title: Annual rent increases
verifies: No petition is required to impose an annual allowable increase; landlords cannot round up to the nearest dollar; worked calculation ($1,500 x 1.6% = $24).

title: Report an unlawful rent increase or request a review of your rent history
verifies: The tenant-facing entry point for challenging an increase and for obtaining a rent-history determination - i.e. the mechanism by which any increase on these units would be scrutinised.

verifies: Official forms referenced throughout this project (571, 572, 573, 354, 361, 302, 322-331).

verifies: The administering agency for the San Francisco Rent Ordinance.

title: Rent Board Portal (Housing Inventory filing, license lookup, fee payment)

title: Cal. Civil Code Sec. 827 - notice of change in terms of tenancy
verifies: Sec. 827(b)(2): 30 days' written notice where the proposed increase is 10% or less of the rent charged at any time in the prior 12 months, alone or combined with other increases. Sec. 827(b)(3)(A): 90 days where it is greater than 10%. Sec. 827(b)(1): service personally or by mail under CCP Sec. 1013.

title: Cal. Civil Code Sec. 1947.12 - Tenant Protection Act of 2019 (AB 1482) rent cap
verifies: Sec. 1947.12(a)(1): cap of 5% plus the percentage change in the cost of living, or 10%, whichever is LOWER, over any 12-month period. Sec. 1947.12(d)(3): EXEMPTION for housing subject to local rent or price control that restricts annual increases to LESS than subdivision (a) - this is why the SF cap, not the state cap, governs these units. Sec. 1947.12(d)(5)(A): the separately-alienable (single-family / condo) exemption is UNAVAILABLE to a REIT, a corporation, or an LLC with a corporate member. Sec. 1947.12(e): notice per Sec. 827. Sec. 1947.12(g)(1)(A)(iv) and (g)(3)(B): the applicable CPI-U is the San Francisco-Oakland-Hayward metropolitan index, measured April to April for increases effective on or after August 1.

title: Cal. Civil Code Sec. 1954.53 - Costa-Hawkins: initial rental rate on vacancy
verifies: Sec. 1954.53(a): an owner may establish the INITIAL rental rate on a new tenancy, subject to exceptions. Sec. 1954.53(b): subdivision (a) includes RENEWAL of the initial hiring by the same tenant/subtenant for the entire period of occupancy AT THE RATE ESTABLISHED FOR THE INITIAL HIRING. Sec. 1954.53(d)(2): a market-rate increase reaches only a lawful sublessee or assignee who did not reside there before 1/1/1996, and only if the original occupant(s) no longer permanently reside there. Sec. 1954.53(d)(3): DOES NOT APPLY to a PARTIAL CHANGE IN OCCUPANCY where one or more occupants under the agreement with the owner remains in lawful possession. Sec. 1954.53(f): serious uncorrected code violations block the provision. Amended by Stats. 2023, Ch. 767 (AB 1620).

title: Cal. Civil Code Sec. 1954.52 - Costa-Hawkins: exemptions
verifies: Sec. 1954.52(a): an owner may set initial and all subsequent rents where the unit has a certificate of occupancy issued after 2/1/1995, was already exempt on/before 2/1/1995 under a local new-construction exemption, or is separately alienable. Sec. 1954.52(d): the section does not apply to a unit with serious health, safety, fire or building code violations cited and unabated for six months or longer preceding the vacancy. Amended by Stats. 2004, Ch. 568, Sec. 4.

title: Cal. Civil Code Sec. 1946.2 - just cause for termination
verifies: The statewide just-cause requirement that accompanies the AB 1482 rent cap (context only - SF Chapter 37 Sec. 37.9 supplies the operative just-cause regime for these units).

title: AB-1482 Tenant Protection Act of 2019 - bill text
verifies: Legislative history of the statewide cap and the exemption structure codified at Civ. Code Sec. 1946.2 and Sec. 1947.12.
